title: Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation for coronary heart disease
authors: Dibben G, de Vries FB, Faulkner J, Oldridge N, Rees K, Stens NA, et al.
followUp: short term 6 to 12 months; medium term above 12 to 36 months; long term above 36 months
population: 107 randomised trials of exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation against no structured exercise in adults with coronary heart disease, mostly after myocardial infarction or revascularisation; mean ages 47 to 81 years; women 17% of participants; search to March 2026
funder: Internal sources: University of Glasgow (time of two authors); Radboud University Medical Centre (time of three authors). External sources: past NIHR Cochrane Infrastructure funding to Cochrane Heart.
authorConflicts: Several authors declare involvement in included trials and took no part in decisions or data extraction for them; one is a health adviser to the Danish Heart Foundation, Ministry of Health and National Board of Health; the others declare none.
result: At 6 to 12 months, exercise-based rehabilitation likely reduced all-cause mortality (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.00; 30 trials, 10,391 participants; number needed to treat 125; moderate certainty), may reduce cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.87, 0.68 to 1.11; moderate certainty), reduced myocardial infarction (RR 0.72, 0.54 to 0.95; 25 trials, 8584 participants; number needed to treat 71; high certainty) and likely reduced all-cause hospital admissions (RR 0.65, 0.51 to 0.82; number needed to treat 17; moderate certainty), with little or no difference in CABG or PCI. Beyond 12 months it was associated with reduced cardiovascular mortality and myocardial infarction. About a quarter of trials predate contemporary optimal medical therapy.
